text:
andrew: ran a 2h flamegraph on host-proxy during a small-req spike, and the hot path is way more host-side than I expected. top 3: HTTP framing + parse, tokenizer, and tiny-message serialization. full stack is ~40% sys/parse overhead. :eyes:

andrew: here's the gist: lots of clients send 1-5 token chunks (mostly streaming chat). that makes continuous syscall/serialize/flush cycles -> CPU churn.

andrew: perf snippet I used: ```perf record -F 200 -g -- ./host-proxy && perf script | FlameGraph/stackcollapse.pl | FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > fg.svg```

andrew: cc @tanya @kevin - thinking we should try coalescing small outgoing chunks at the proxy and canonicalize tokenization at ingress to avoid duplicate work.

tanya: nice find. do you have breakdown http1 vs grpc (http2) costs? earlier notes said http2 multiplexing helped, but if each stream is tiny it still hits framing/serialize cost.

andrew: good q — I split traces by transport. HTTP/1.1 keepalive has higher per-connection setup cost but lower per-frame overhead vs h2 for very small msgs; gRPC/h2 shows cost in stream state machine and HPACK encode/decode. both lose when message count is high and payload tiny.

kevin: this meshes with batching heuristics work — runtime assumes client will amortize tokens per request. but the SDK (JS + mobile) aggressively flushes on every intermediate chunk for latency. that kills throughput.

kevin: short-term we can implement a configurable coalescer in host-proxy: buffer up to N bytes or M ms before flush unless client sets low-latency flag. default N=1024, M=12ms? that'll reduce syscall/serialize rate w/o hurting tail-latency much.

maria: also saw KV-cache churn related to partial-tokenization mismatch. when clients use different tokenizers (js vs python unicode normalizations) the prefix keys don't match and we get cache misses + extra host tokenization calls.

maria: proposal: move to canonical UTF-normalize + fastBPE apply on the ingress path once, then store canonicalized prefix key in KV cache. that avoids re-tokenizing on downstream workers.

andrew: +1. doing tokenization once at the proxy also reduces duplicated CPU across worker pool. question: cost of canonicalization itself vs savings? my perf suggests canonicalize is ~0.5-0.8ms per request but avoids ~2-3 ms repeated work when K workers would otherwise redo it. break-even at K=2.

tanya: sounds promising. we should be careful about privacy: tokenization is deterministic but we must not persist raw user text. store only prefix-ids/hashed keys in cache with short TTL. encrypt at rest as usual.

kevin: implementation sketch for coalescer (host-proxy): ```
// pseudo
buf = []
start = now()
while not end_of_stream:
  chunk = read_in()
  buf.append(chunk)
  if buf.size >= 1024 or now() - start >= 0.012 or chunk.flags.contains("flush"):
    emit(concat(buf))
    buf.clear()
    start = now()
```

kevin: also add header hints: `x-rr-coalesce: aggressive|balanced|none` so customers can opt out. default balanced.

maria: for KV keys I'd propose: `sha256(prefix_ids|model|norm_version)` so runtime can lookup by prefix ids directly. don't keep source text. TTL 30s for streaming sessions.

andrew: got a quick microbench: coalescer reduces syscalls by ~60% and overall host CPU by ~22% for chat-like traces. tail p99 latency increased by ~0.8ms in the worst case for our balanced config.

tanya: good tradeoff. let's gate behind a feature flag and run A/B on staging. Perf-bot, can you schedule a cluster test with 1k concurrent chat streams that flush frequently?

perf-bot: scheduled perf-run id=proj-host-coalesce-2026-03-20, cluster=staging-3, concurrency=1000, duration=30m, config=coalesce-balanced vs baseline. ETA 2026-03-20T14:00Z.

kevin: also need to update client SDKs docs and add `x-rr-coalesce` header support. mobile SDK should default to conservative flush to play nicely.

maria: one more: tokenizer integration — let's upstream a small C binding for our fastBPE tokenizer into host-proxy so canonicalization costs drop to ~0.2ms. that buys more wins. I'll draft the binding.

andrew: action items:
- kevin: prototype coalescer in host-proxy (PR branch: coalesce-small-chunks)
- maria: implement fastBPE C binding + canonicalize path
- tanya: run staged A/B and validate p50/p95/p99 and CPU savings
- perf-bot: run scheduled perf-run and post results in this thread

kevin: I'll open the PR today with perf harness and minimal flagging.

maria: starting tokenizer binding PR, will ping for review when initial benchmarks are in.

tanya: thanks all. if we can get ~15-25% host CPU reduction without hurting user p99, this is a big win for Dedicated cost targets. :rocket:

deploy-bot: reminder: feature flags required for staging rollouts. create FF: host_coalesce_balanced (type=boolean, default=false). created by tanya.

andrew: I'll follow up with flamegraphs of before/after once coalescer PR is up. cheers.
